name: North Fork of Roanoke

known.via: English Wikipedia "North Fork of Roanoke AVA"

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, hot summer

climate: Seasons this warm ripen Chardonnay, Cabernet Franc, Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon and Sauvignon Blanc fully without cooking off their freshness.
Chardonnay, Cabernet Franc, Merlot and Cabernet Sauvignon sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.

soil.rock: Shale and mudstone are fine-grained rocks that hold heat well and are moderately fertile.
soil.top: The topsoil stores water through dry spells, but stays wet and cold after rain, which slows ripening and can swell the grapes. It is very acid, which locks up nutrients, so growers spread lime to raise the pH.

land: The high ground runs about 3°F cooler than the low ground. Higher vineyards ripen later and keep more acidity, so one grape can make lighter or richer wine here depending on height.
Much of it is steep. Cold air and rain run off, so frost and waterlogging are rare and soils stay thin, keeping yields low. Steep rows are slow and costly to work, often by hand.

winkler: Early and mid-season grapes make good wine.
